newsitem.title: USA: CBOT yield-spread contracts off to good start.
newsitem.headline: CBOT yield-spread contracts off to good start.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade's (CBOT) new Treasury yield curve spread futures and options saw healthy interest on their first day of trading on Friday, traders and exchange officials said.
"At the start, it was hard to get a quote because every firm was looking for a quote," said a brokerage trader on the CBOT trading floor. "But within minutes, it was actually okay."
Traders said volume was higher than many people had anticipated, particularly when taking into account a relatively stable underlying Treasuries market.
According to CBOT, volume for the spread futures totalled about 2,000 contracts, while turnover in options was about 1,500. Actual figures will be available Monday.
Kyle Petersen, vice president of Sakura Dellsher Inc, said inter-dealer trading probably accounted for most of the initial volume.

"It's going to take some time for everybody to feel comfortable with this thing, but I think there is a lot of interest," he said. "End-users are sitting on the sidelines right now to see the volume pick up and make sure they feel confident in the way they're priced."

Traders said November 2-30 year spread futures ZDX6 were probably the most actively traded. The contract closed at 10088 (88 basis-point positive spread) after opening at 10095 and gradually easing to a low of 10087.
"I guess some guys were feeling it out, trying to figure out how to price this," Petersen said of the relatively wide range compared with the equivalent cash Treasuries spread.
Looking ahead, traders said quarterly refunding in early November could be a major catalyst for wider participation.
"By the time we get to the refunding, I think we're going to see some good volume," Petersen said.

The new CBOT contracts cover spreads between any combination of two-, three-, five-, 10- and 30-year points on the yield curve, based on the most actively traded -- or "on-the-run" -- Treasury issues.

"Users will be able to isolate the slope of the yield curve with just one transaction, saving time and money," CBOT Chairman Patrick Arbor said in a statement. "Further, the risk reward profiles of these options cannot be replicated using traditional fixed income instruments."
